chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: 'I went to see Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him, "O son of the Prophet! The people say that you have accepted the succession to the throne while showing asceticism in the world."'

He (peace be upon him) replied: 'God knows my dislike for that. When I was given the choice between accepting it and being killed, I chose acceptance over death. Woe to them! Do they not know that Joseph (peace be upon him) was a Prophet and Messenger, and when necessity drove him to manage the storehouses of the Aziz, he said to him, "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land; indeed, I am a knowing guardian." Necessity drove me to accept it under compulsion and coercion after being on the verge of death.'
With the condition that I did not enter this affair except as one who has no interest in it. To God is the complaint made, and He is the One sought for help.

key_terms.فَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمُشْتَكَى: To God is the complaint made

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Rida accept the Caliphate from Al-Ma'mun if he disliked it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Rida (a.s.) clarifying that his acceptance of Al-Ma'mun’s forced designation (al-khuruj bi-l-qasr) was a strategic necessity to preserve the Imamat from extinction, rather than a voluntary acquisition of political power. By invoking Prophet Joseph’s (a.s.) stewardship of Egypt’s granaries under duress, the Imam establishes a theological precedent for the Imams' temporary engagement with the ruling caliphate to safeguard the community and the lineage of prophethood. This narrative underscores the concept of 'compelled entry' (dakhul al-ikrah), where the Imam remains spiritually detached from the worldly authority he temporarily inhabits.
